cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Told You Enough
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest while repeatedly narrowing what honesty requires and which details count.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I'll be honest about your missing donation box. You asked where I went; I said the bank.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you take the box there?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Yes. You didn't ask what was inside.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Was the money still in it when you arrived?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At the car park, yes. If you mean the counter, that's a different arrival.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 promises honesty under A's decision, A3 limits the question to the box rather than contents, and A5 rules two meanings of arrival.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 box question gets A3 yes plus contents loophole; B4 closes that loophole and A5 opens the location distinction.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 refine the inquiry in direct response to A's evasions.

heightening.evidence: A5 narrows arrival after B4 specifically asks about money on arrival, extending the same game.

specificity.evidence: A1 missing donation box and bank, A5 car park and counter, establish exact objects and locations.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 different arrival is an earned semantic retreat, not a disconnected joke.
